_about: The covenant hub (plan 7.6f), the second round of hubs after the first fifteen. Covenant is one family: the Hebrew noun בְּרִית (263 verses) and the Greek noun διαθήκη (30), which the Greek Old Testament uses for it and the New Testament for the covenants it names. There is no verb of the family: the Hebrew says a covenant is 'cut' (כָּרַת), 'established' (קוּם), 'kept' (שָׁמַר), 'remembered' (זָכַר), 'broken' (פָּרַר), so the verb rows are noun rows by the verb whose object the covenant is (object_of, from the frames), with the verses the frames lack added by hand. Rows as in love.json, righteousness.json and forgiveness.json: a verse sits in every row it fits (match: all); the covenants by name (Noah, Abraham, Sinai, David, Levi) and the verb rows are by hand through 'add', which keeps a verse only where the covenant word really stands in it, so a mistyped reference falls out instead of showing a verse without the word. The contested points are set side by side, in the alphabetical order of their labels, each with the same no-side sentence: how the covenants relate (one covenant in several forms, or several; the old and the new; Israel and the church). The page names no covenant scheme and no dispensation. Built by tools/concepts/hub_build.py into out/concept-hubs/covenant.json.

titles.noun: What the text says of the covenant

_words_why: בְּרִית and διαθήκη, together because the Greek Old Testament renders the one by the other and the New Testament quotes it so (Heb 8:8-12 quotes Jer 31:31-34), but the hub never says they are one word: the Hebrew is 'covenant', 'treaty', 'alliance'; the Greek is also 'will', which the Berean prints at Heb 9:16-17 (its own row, with a note). Left out of the words as different: אָלָה and שְׁבוּעָה (oath), which stand beside the covenant in a row of their own, and the verbs of the idiom (כָּרַת, קוּם, שָׁמַר, זָכַר, פָּרַר), which are not the word covenant. Verses where the Berean prints 'covenant' and the Greek has no noun (Heb 8:7, 8:13, 9:1, 9:18: 'the first', 'new', and the noun understood) are not in the hub, because no word of the family stands in them; the note of 'A new covenant' says so. Isa 42:6 ('a covenant for the people', לִ + בְרִית) is likewise not seen by the builder (the word-by-word text splits the prefix) and is named in the report.
_sense_why: Empty, as holiness: every use of בְּרִית is the one word, whether the Berean prints covenant, treaty, alliance or allies, and the rows divide the uses by what the covenant is about. A gloss rule would have dropped the treaty verses (Josh 9, 1 Kgs 15:19) that the Hebrew puts in the same word as Sinai. Measured: 263 of 263 Hebrew verses and 30 of 30 Greek verses kept, none dropped.

others._why: Words the English also renders covenant, treaty or alliance that are not בְּרִית or διαθήκη, named apart with their verses and never handed over as the same word.
others.title: Other words translated “covenant”, “treaty”, “alliance”

h3772.note: כָּרַת means “cut”, the verb of the idiom “cut a covenant”. In these five verses it stands alone, with no word for covenant, and the Berean supplies “covenant” or “treaty”; so they are not in the rows, which stand on the noun בְּרִית.

_own_words_why: One from each of the covenants the text names (Noah, Abraham, Sinai, David, the new) and Gal 3:17 beside Heb 8:13, which readers part on; the card's own first four words are the Noah verses alone. Heb 8:13 has no Greek noun for covenant (see _words_why), so it is shown here as a key verse and is in no row.

rows.label: With Noah and every living creature
rows.note: Gen 6:18 and 9:9 say “you”: God's speech to Noah, who is named in Gen 6:8 and 9:8.
rows._why: by hand, through 'add': the verses of the flood story that say covenant. Gen 9:10 (the creatures) has no word for covenant and is not in the hub.

rows.label: With the day and the night, the beasts, the stones, one's eyes, death
rows.note: Isa 28:15 and 28:18 are the words of leaders who say “We have made a covenant with death”; 28:18 says “Your covenant with death will be dissolved”. The page says no more of them.
rows._why: by hand: a covenant said of what is not a person, in the text's own words (Jer 33:20, 33:25 'My covenant with the day and the night'; Hos 2:18 the beasts of the field; Job 5:23 the stones; Job 31:1 'with my eyes'; Job 41:4 Leviathan; Isa 28:15, 28:18 'a covenant with death')

rows.label: With Abram, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob

not_verses.Gen.21.27: Abraham and Abimelech make a covenant between themselves: it stands in 'Between people and nations'
not_verses.Gen.14.13: Abram's allies, men bound to him by treaty: it stands in 'Between people and nations'

rows.note: Gen 17:2-14 is God's speech to Abram, named in 17:1 and renamed Abraham in 17:5; the verses of it that say covenant are here though they say “you”, not the name. Jacob is named with them in Exod 2:24, Lev 26:42, 2 Kgs 13:23, 1 Chr 16:17 and Ps 105:10.
rows._why: by the names in the verse (Abraham, Abram, Isaac), with the Genesis 15 and 17 verses and the verses that name Jacob beside them added by hand, each only where the verse has the covenant word. Exod 6:4 ('I also established My covenant with them') is God's speech with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob named in 6:3.

rows.label: Egypt, Sinai, Horeb and Moses

not_verses.Gen.15.18: 'the river of Egypt' marks the land; the covenant is with Abram and stands in 'With Abraham, Isaac and Jacob'
not_verses.Ezek.17.15: Zedekiah sends envoys to Egypt: a covenant between a king and Babylon, in 'Between people and nations'
not_verses.Hos.12.1: Ephraim makes a covenant with Assyria and takes oil to Egypt: in 'Between people and nations'

rows._why: the verses that name Egypt, Sinai, Horeb or Moses beside the covenant, with the Exodus and Deuteronomy verses that say it without those names added by hand (Exod 19:5 'keep My covenant', 24:7-8 the book and the blood, 34:10-28, Deut 4:13 the tablets, 5:2, 9:9-15). The three verses with Egypt only as a place are held out (not_verses).

rows.label: Covenants made in Moab, at Shechem and in the days of Jehoiada, Asa, Hezekiah, Josiah and Ezra
rows.note: Several of these verses say “the king” or “they”, not the name: 2 Kgs 23:3 is Josiah's (named in 23:1), 2 Chr 15:12 is Asa's (named in 15:8), and 2 Chr 29:10 is Hezekiah's (named in 29:1).
rows._why: by hand: the covenants the text says were made in a later hour, each in its own words ('besides the covenant He had made at Horeb', Deut 29:1; 'made a covenant with the people that day at Shechem', Josh 24:25; 'to make a covenant with the LORD', 2 Chr 29:10). The verses that only read or keep the Book of the Covenant (2 Kgs 23:2, 2 Chr 34:30, Deut 29:9, 29:21) are not here; they say read or keep, not made.

rows.label: David
rows.note: 2 Sam 23:5 says “my house” and “me”: it is David's own speech, his last words, named in 23:1.
rows._why: by hand: the verses where the covenant is David's. 2 Sam 5:3 (David and the elders) and 1 Sam 18:3, 20:8 (David and Jonathan) are covenants between people and stand in 'Between people and nations'.

rows.label: Levi, Phinehas and the priests
rows.note: Several of these verses say “him” or “you”, not the name: Num 25:12-13 speak of Phinehas (named in 25:11), Mal 2:5 of Levi (named in 2:4), Deut 33:9 is Moses' blessing of Levi (33:8), and Num 18:19 is said to Aaron and his sons (18:1).
rows._why: by hand: 'My covenant of peace' to Phinehas (Num 25:12-13), 'My covenant with Levi' (Mal 2:4-8), 'the covenant of the priesthood' (Neh 13:29), Levi's keeping of it (Deut 33:9), the Levitical priests with David (Jer 33:21), and the covenant of salt for the priests' portion (Num 18:19, spoken to Aaron and his sons). Lev 24:8 (the Sabbath bread, 'a permanent covenant' for the Israelites) names no priest and is under 'An everlasting covenant'.

rows.label: A new covenant; the first covenant, the old covenant
rows.note: The text's own phrases: “a new covenant” in the Hebrew (Jer 31:31) and in the Greek that quotes it (Heb 8:8, 9:15, 12:24), in the words over the cup (Luke 22:20; 1 Cor 11:25) and in Paul's ministry (2 Cor 3:6); and “the first covenant” (Heb 9:15) and “the old covenant” (2 Cor 3:14). In Heb 8:7, 8:13, 9:1 and 9:18 the Berean prints “covenant” where the Greek says only “the first” or “new” and has no noun, so those verses are not counted in this hub; Heb 8:13 is among its key verses. The Hebrew text says “a new covenant” only at Jer 31:31; “the old covenant” (2 Cor 3:14) and “the first covenant” (Heb 9:15) are phrases of Paul and of Hebrews, not of the Hebrew Scriptures. Jer 31:31-33 also stands in the rows on Egypt, Israel, the law, the heart, and making and breaking the covenant, so the passage can be read in sequence. How the new covenant stands to the covenants before it -- one covenant renewed, or another -- and to whom it is made, Israel or the church, is a point on which Christian traditions part, and the page takes no side. This row and the rows beside it are listed in the alphabetical order of their labels and carry no ranking.
rows._why: the Greek 'new' (καινός, νέος), 'first' (πρῶτος) or 'old' (παλαιός), or the Hebrew חָדָשׁ, beside the covenant noun. Was two rows ('A new covenant' 7, 'The first covenant, the old covenant' 2): merged, since the 'first' and 'old' verses are the two the Greek puts beside the noun and a two-verse row was too small to stand alone. Isa 42:6, 49:8, 55:3, 59:21, 61:8, Jer 32:40, Ezek 34:25, 37:26 do not say 'new' and are under 'everlasting', 'peace' or the other rows.

rows.label: An everlasting covenant; a covenant of peace
rows.note: The text's own phrases: “an everlasting covenant” of Noah, of Abraham, of David, of the priests, of the LORD with His people, and in Heb 13:20 “the blood of the eternal covenant”; and “My covenant of peace”. These are two phrases, not one: “everlasting” is the Hebrew עוֹלָם, “peace” is שָׁלוֹם, and the row holds the verses of either. Heb 13:20 is in Greek, and its word for “eternal” is αἰώνιος, a different word from the Hebrew. Where Christian traditions part on how the covenants that are called everlasting stand to one another and to the new covenant, the page takes no side. This row and the rows beside it are listed in the alphabetical order of their labels and carry no ranking.
rows._why: עוֹלָם and αἰώνιος beside the covenant noun, and שָׁלוֹם and εἰρήνη (Isa 54:10, Ezek 34:25, 37:26); Num 25:12, Mal 2:5 ('a covenant of life and peace'), Num 18:19 ('a permanent covenant of salt') and Ps 111:9 ('commanded His covenant forever') are added by hand because the word sits two words away or in another clause. The Berean's 'everlasting', 'permanent', 'lasting', 'forever' and 'eternal' are all the one עוֹלָם / αἰώνιος.

rows.label: The covenant and foreigners, strangers, the nations

not_verses.Josh.3.17: גּוֹי is 'nation' and means Israel crossing the Jordan
not_verses.Deut.31.16: נֵכָר is 'foreign gods', not foreigners as people

rows.note: The verses that name the foreigner, the stranger or the nations beside the covenant: the many nations of Abraham (Gen 17:4), foreigners who “hold fast to My covenant” (Isa 56:6), the foreigner as well as the native-born at Ebal (Josh 8:33), foreigners brought into the sanctuary (Ezek 44:7), and “strangers to the covenants of promise” (Eph 2:12). Where Christian traditions part on how the nations and Israel stand to the covenants, the page takes no side. This row and the rows beside it are listed in the alphabetical order of their labels and carry no ranking.
rows._why: the words גּוֹי, גֵּר, נֵכָר, ἔθνος, ξένος in the verse, read from the word-by-word text. Three verses held out (not_verses) where the word is 'nation' for Israel or 'foreign' of gods. Isa 42:6 ('a covenant for the people and a light to the nations') would stand here but is not seen by the builder.

rows.label: The covenant and Israel, Judah
rows.note: The verses that name Israel or Judah beside the covenant, among them the covenant made “with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah” (Jer 31:31, quoted at Heb 8:8) and the covenants that “belong to the Israelites” (Rom 9:4). Where Christian traditions part on whom the covenants are with, and how Israel and the church stand to them, the page takes no side. This row and the rows beside it are listed in the alphabetical order of their labels and carry no ranking.
rows._why: the words יִשְׂרָאֵל, יְהוּדָה, Ἰσραήλ, Ἰσραηλίτης in the verse. A big row on purpose: the Hebrew puts the people in many covenant verses, and a smaller one would hide how often.

rows.label: The covenant and the law, the commandments, the promise
rows.note: The verses that name the law, the commandments, the statutes or the promise beside the covenant, among them Gal 3:17 (“The law that came 430 years later does not revoke the covenant previously established by God, so as to nullify the promise”) and Eph 2:12 (“the covenants of promise”). Where Christian traditions part on how the law and the promise stand to the covenants, the page takes no side. This row and the rows beside it are listed in the alphabetical order of their labels and carry no ranking.
rows._why: the Hebrew law words (תּוֹרָה, מִצְוָה, חֹק, חֻקָּה, פִּקּוּד, עֵדוּת) and the Greek (νόμος, ἐντολή, ἐπαγγελία, ἐπαγγέλλομαι) in the verse

rows.label: The covenants, two covenants, a better covenant; Jesus its guarantor and mediator
rows.note: The plural and the comparative, in the text's own words: “the covenants” (Rom 9:4), “the covenants of promise” (Eph 2:12), “two covenants” (Gal 4:24), “a better covenant” (Heb 7:22, 8:6), “the mediator of a new covenant” (Heb 9:15, 12:24). Heb 7:22, 8:6 and 12:24 name Jesus, Heb 9:15 Christ. Gal 4:24 gives “two covenants” in what the Berean calls illustrations (the Greek is ἀλληγορούμενα) of Hagar and Sinai, not as a count of the covenants; the plural in Rom 9:4 and Eph 2:12 gives no number. “Guarantor” is Heb 7:22 only; “mediator” is Heb 8:6, 9:15, 12:24. How many covenants the Bible holds, and how they relate, is a point on which Christian traditions part, and the page takes no side. This row and the rows beside it are listed in the alphabetical order of their labels and carry no ranking.
rows._why: by hand (the plural and the comparative are not a word the builder can read): the verses that count the covenants or call one better. The four Hebrews verses are those where the text itself names Jesus or Christ with the covenant, as the divine persons are filled (pick, never a rule).

rows.label: Written on the heart; My Spirit and My words; the Spirit, not the letter
rows.note: Three things, each in its own verses. “I will put My laws in their minds and inscribe them on their hearts” (Jer 31:33; Heb 8:10; 10:16) says nothing of the Spirit. “My Spirit who is upon you, and My words that I have put in your mouth” (Isa 59:21) says nothing of the heart. “Not of the letter but of the Spirit” (2 Cor 3:6) sets the Spirit against the letter. Where Christian traditions part on how these stand to the other covenants and to whom they are made, the page takes no side. This row and the rows beside it are listed in the alphabetical order of their labels and carry no ranking.
rows._why: by hand: five verses that say what is written or put (the heart, the mind, the Spirit, the words). It is the last of the block because W follows A and T in the labels' alphabetical order.

rows.label: The blood of the covenant, the cup, the sacrifice

not_verses.Dan.9.27: he will put an end to sacrifice and offering: no blood or cup, and beside Matt 26:28 it hints at a link the text does not state; it stands in 'Every other use' (ruled 2026-10-25)
not_verses.Exod.34.15: the sacrifice is the neighbours' to their gods ('you eat of his sacrifice'): a prohibition, in 'Between people and nations'
not_verses.Ezek.44.7: blood and fat offered by foreigners in the sanctuary, while 'breaking My covenant': not the blood of the covenant

rows.note: The Hebrew verses first: “Behold the blood of the covenant” (Exod 24:8), “because of the blood of My covenant” (Zech 9:11), “a covenant with Me by sacrifice” (Ps 50:5). Then the Greek: “My blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many” (Matt 26:28), “This cup is the new covenant in My blood” (Luke 22:20; 1 Cor 11:25). What a sacrifice does, and whether the Lord's Supper is a sacrifice or a memorial, are points on which Christian traditions part, and the page takes no side.
rows._why: the words for blood, cup, sacrifice and offering in the verse (דָּם, αἷμα, ποτήριον, כּוֹס, זֶבַח, θυσία, προσφορά). The cup in 1 Cor 11:25 is joined with 'in remembrance of Me' in the verse; the page does not read it. Three verses held out where the sacrifice or blood is not the covenant's (Dan 9:27 since the 2026-10-25 ruling).

rows.label: The sign of the covenant: the rainbow and circumcision

not_verses.Josh.8.33: מוּל is 'in front of' here, the same letters as circumcise; nothing is circumcised

rows._why: the words sign and circumcise in the verse (אוֹת, σημεῖον, מוּל, περιτομή, περιτέμνω): Gen 9:12-13, 9:17 the rainbow, Gen 17:10-14 circumcision, Acts 7:8 'the covenant of circumcision'. The Sabbath is the covenant's 'sign' at Exod 31:13-17, but only 31:16 carries the covenant word ('a permanent covenant') and it stands under 'An everlasting covenant'; Josh 8:33 is held out where מוּל is a preposition.

rows.label: The ark, the tablets and the book of the covenant
rows._why: the ark (אֲרוֹן, κιβωτός), the tablets (לוּחַ, πλάξ) or the book (סֵפֶר, βιβλίον) next to the covenant noun, as 'the ark of the covenant'

rows.label: The covenant and loving devotion, mercy
rows.note: In Neh 9:32 the Hebrew has “the covenant and the steadfast love” (בְּרִית and חֶסֶד), and the Berean prints “gracious covenant”.
rows._why: חֶסֶד (the Berean's 'loving devotion', 'steadfast love') or ἔλεος in the verse: 'keeps His covenant of loving devotion' (Deut 7:9), 'to show mercy ... and to remember His holy covenant' (Luke 1:72)

rows.label: The covenant with an oath or a curse
rows._why: the words for swearing, oath and curse in the verse. אָלָה is 'curse' and 'oath' in one word (Deut 29:12, 'the oath', 29:21, 'the curses'); the label says both.

rows.label: Between people and nations: made, sworn and forbidden
rows.note: One Hebrew word, בְּרִית, which the Berean prints “covenant”, “treaty” or “alliance”. Exod 23:32 and Deut 7:2 name the peoples of the land (Canaan) as those with whom no covenant, no treaty, is to be made; Josh 9 is the Gibeonites' covenant, and Joshua says to them “Why did you deceive us” (9:22). Ps 83:5 is a covenant formed against God. The verses are set as the text states them.
rows._why: by hand: a covenant between people or kings, made (Abraham and Abimelech, David and Jonathan, Solomon and Hiram, Ahab and Ben-Hadad), broken (Zedekiah, Ezek 17) or forbidden ('You shall make no covenant with them', Exod 23:32, 34:12, Deut 7:2, Judg 2:2); the verses say 'covenant' of an agreement between people in the same word as Sinai. Dan 11:22 ('the prince of the covenant') is not here: it is not plainly an agreement between people.

rows.label: Where the Berean prints “will”
rows.note: The same Greek word, διαθήκη, that the Berean prints “covenant” in the rest of its verses, among them Gal 3:15 (“Even a human covenant, once it is ratified, cannot be canceled or amended”) and Heb 9:15 and 9:18 just before and after. In Heb 9:16-17 it prints “will” (“In the case of a will, it is necessary to establish the death of the one who made it”). Whether the Greek means a will, a covenant, or both in these verses is a question translators answer differently, and the page does not choose.
rows._why: rule 6 of the brief: never present one sense of a word as its whole. A two-verse row is kept on purpose, because the text sets it apart: one Greek word, two English words, inside one passage (Heb 9:15-18). Gal 3:15 first stood here and was taken out: the Berean prints 'covenant' there.

rows.label: Make, establish, give a covenant
rows.note: The Hebrew idiom for making a covenant is literally “cut” (כָּרַת); the Berean prints “make”. The other verbs are “establish”, “give”, “set”, and the Greek διατίθημι. Many of these verses also stand under the named covenants above (Noah, Abraham, Sinai and the rest), so the two sets overlap; 87 is a count of verses, not of covenants.
rows._why: the covenant as the object of כָּרַת 'cut' (the idiom), קוּם 'establish', נָתַן 'give', שִׂים 'set', בּוֹא 'bring', and the Greek διατίθημι, from the frames; the verses the frames miss (the Hebrew hiphil 'I established', Gen 17:7, 17:19, 17:21, Exod 6:4, Lev 26:9, Deut 8:18; and 2 Chr 23:1, Isa 49:8, Ezek 16:60, 16:62) are added by hand

rows.label: Keep, observe, hold fast to the covenant

not_verses.2Sam.23.5: 'ordered and secured in every part' is the covenant guarded, not a person keeping it

rows.note: The text's own verbs: “keep My covenant” (Gen 17:9; Exod 19:5), “observe” (Deut 33:9), “hold fast” (Isa 56:4, 56:6), and in the negative “they did not keep” (Ps 78:10). The page says nothing of what keeping earns or whether it can be lost; the verses are set as they stand.
rows._why: the covenant as the object of שָׁמַר 'keep', נָצַר 'observe', חָזַק 'hold fast' and the Greek τηρέω, φυλάσσω; Isa 56:4, 56:6 ('hold fast to My covenant', the verb takes the covenant after a preposition) and Deut 29:9 ('keep the words of this covenant') added by hand. 2 Sam 23:5 held out: the covenant is 'secured', not kept by someone.

rows.label: Remember, forget the covenant
rows._why: the covenant as the object of זָכַר 'remember' (Gen 9:15, Exod 2:24, Ps 105:8, Luke 1:72) and of שָׁכַח 'forget' (Deut 4:23, Prov 2:17, 2 Kgs 17:38); Luke 1:72 added (the Greek verb is an infinitive the frames do not carry)

rows.label: Broken, transgressed, forsaken, despised, profaned, corrupted; “did not continue in”
rows.note: Hos 6:7 says “like Adam, have transgressed the covenant”; the page does not decide who or what Adam is there.
rows._why: the covenant as the object of פָּרַר 'break', עָבַר 'transgress', עָזַב 'forsake', חָלַל 'profane', בָּזָה 'despise', שָׁחַת 'corrupt', מָאַס 'reject', נָאַר 'renounce', from the frames; the frames carry 14 of the verses, and the rest (the hiphil 'He has broken', the infinitives 'to break', the passives) are added by hand, each only where the verse has the covenant word. Heb 8:9 ('they did not continue in My covenant') is added: the verb takes the covenant after 'in'. Hos 6:7 is included in the text's own words ('like Adam'); the page says nothing of who Adam is there.

rows.label: Every other use
rows.note: What no other row takes, among it Rom 11:27, “And this is My covenant with them when I take away their sins”, the verse after “all Israel will be saved” (Rom 11:26). Where Christian traditions part on whom “them” is, and on how this stands to the covenants, the page takes no side. Also here: Mal 2:14, “your wife by covenant”, and Mal 3:1, “the Messenger of the covenant”; the page says no more of either. Dan 9:27 names a covenant confirmed with many and an end put to sacrifice and offering; readers part on who “he” is, and the page does not choose. The Hebrew word בְּרִית stands beside words of marriage in Mal 2:14 (“your wife by covenant”), in Prov 2:17 (“the covenant of her God”, said of a woman who abandons “the partner of her youth”) and in Ezek 16:8 (the LORD “entered into a covenant with you, and you became Mine”). Mal 2:14 is here; Prov 2:17 shows in “Remember, forget the covenant” and Ezek 16:8 in “The covenant with an oath or a curse”. The page does not say whether Prov 2:17 means a marriage or the covenant with God.
